title: Compact field notes: fast-inference heuristics & quick experiments
content:
Quick context / goal:
- Personal scratchpad for cheap, pragmatic experiments to drop per-token cost and tail latency on customer chat workloads (150–2k token turns). Not a polished doc; notes to self.

Topline heuristics (short):
- Prefer small quantized variants for long-turn recall workloads where latency dominates; use 16-bit / bf16 on dedicated for short-turn latency-sensitive routes only.
- Turn on prefix KV caching for repeated-session flows; invalidate on model-rollout or system prompt change.
- Use adaptive batching window: 1–3 ms base for premium tier, 8–20 ms for bulk/async routes. Tune per-route.
- Fall back to a smaller model (or depth-limited decoding) when observed median latency > SLO for 5 consecutive mins.

Papers & quick takeaways (skimmed):
- FlashAttention family (fast attention kernels): big win on dense attention for longer contexts; always check kernel availability for chosen hardware before switching. When using flash kernels, benchmark end-to-end with KV caching enabled because memory layout changes can impact perf.
- QLoRA / PTQ notes: mixed results — 4-bit quant gives big memory wins, but for some instruction-tuned models we saw subtle quality regressions on rare-entity retention. Add small eval set focusing on entity recall before shipping.
- ALiBi / relative position biases: simpler for streaming long-context; reduces need for re-embedding long prefixes. Works well with attention-sparse strategies.
- KV-sharding papers & MoE routing: promising for horizontal scaling across GPU islands, but increases routing complexity and tail latency jitter. Keep as mid-term.

Fast experiments to run (priority order):
1) Rolling-bench: reproduce one hosted customer 95th latency baseline vs: (a) KV caching on; (b) KV caching + 4-bit activation quant; (c) smaller model fallback. Measure: p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, quality on 10 targeted prompts.
2) Adaptive-batch window simulation: synthetic trace of session arrivals (70% short, 30% long). Sweep window 1,3,5,10,20 ms. Track latency SLO breaches and effective tokens/sec.
3) Quick probe: partial-decoder trick — cap max new tokens to 64 for initial response, stream rest on release. Check UX regressions.
4) Canary rollout script: when new model deployed, compare top-1 token divergence on canonical prompt set; if > 2% for more than 3 routes, rollback.

Short implementation notes (practical):
- KV cache eviction: use LRU per-session with a soft TTL (30m) and hard TTL (6h). For private deployments, expose TTL knob in config.
- Batching: keep per-GPU batch queues sharded by request size bucketing (0-128, 129-512, 512+ tokens). Avoid mixing tiny and giant requests in same kernel call.
- Prefetch kernels: warm top-k kernels on cold-start by replaying a small warmup trace after deploy. Saves 30–80 ms on first user.
- Monitoring: add token-level cost attribution in traces (token_count * model_unit_cost) and align to request metadata (route, customer tier).

Mini playbook: when p95 spikes:
- Quick triage: are spikes correlated with a single customer or route? (if yes -> route-level rollback)
- Check if new model variant rolled within 30 min -> canary mismatch?
- Check for degraded kernel fallback or OOM events (drivers often emit noisy SRE logs)
- If global: increase batching window for 10m and enable smaller-model fallback for low-priority traffic.

Open questions / fuzzy bits to test:
- How aggressive can we be with 3-bit PTQ for Llama-derived models before hallucination rises measurably? Need a small NER recall eval set.
- What's the UX tradeoff for initial truncated outputs (cap to 64) vs. full streaming? Do users complain about missing context?
- Latency tail sources: queuing vs kernel variance vs network (TLS) — need to add microbench marks in path to attribute.

Notes to self (todo):
- Build a 10-prompt evaluation focused on named-entity continuity (customers 1–3 real flows).
- Add prometheus panel: tokens/sec, avg_batch_size, kernel_miss_rate, kv_cache_hit_rate per model.
- Draft a canary policy doc for product review (link to CONFLUENCE-6789).

Random heuristics I like (cribbed from past runs):
- If >40% of requests are single-token prompts (e.g., search-ish), push them to a tiny reranker model and then only call the big model for top-k.
- Prefer deterministic greedy decode for internal pipeline stages (retrieval selection) to reduce compute variance.

Quick links I referred to while sketching: (save for proper curation)
- FlashAttention repo / kernel notes (github.com/flash-attention)
- QLoRA overview blog (huggingface.co/blog/qlora)
- ALiBi paper notes (search: ALiBi attention biases)

Micro-risks / warnings:
- Quantize-and-serve path is sensitive to tokenizer mismatches (spaces/prefix bytes). Always test token-level alignment between training quant artifacts and runtime tokenizer.
- Private deploys: KMS latency can leak into request median if keys are fetched per-request; ensure caching at connection layer.

Exit lines:
- Keep this lightweight. Move the good bits into an ops-runbook once experiments produce stable deltas.
- Ping Avi / Samir when I have initial rolling-bench outputs (~2 days).

---
(scratch ends)
